R261.note: Correctly narrows supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken, matching the authenticate() cast.

R262.note: Only fixes the minor off-by-one in write_field; misses the actual sink named by the case (packet_buffer.c passes MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY=256 to write_field instead of the real malloc(requestedCapacity) size), so the stale-capacity OOB write remains fully exploitable whenever requestedCapacity < 256.

R263.note: Adds correct overflow-safe bounds check before subspan(); signature and return behavior preserved.

R264.note: Correctly swaps the inverted branches so admins get all orders and non-admins get only their own.

R265.note: Standard parameterized SqlCommand fix, preserves query semantics.

R267.note: strnlen bounded to sizeof(name) closes the OOB read and satisfies the stated contract (existing length preserved, flags never read).

R268.note: strlcat with explicit destination size closes the overflow; both original bound checks preserved.

R269.note: Reproduced against Python 3.13 smtplib: putcmd() already rejects embedded CR/LF identically whether called via docmd() or via sendmail()'s internal mail()/rcpt(), so switching APIs does not verifiably add closure for the CRLF payload the write-up describes as the exploit.

R270.note: std::array::at() bounds-checks and throws on invalid slot, matching the contract's 'rejected or reported' requirement.

R271.note: secrets.choice() replacement preserves the 32-char alphanumeric token format and storage order per contract.

R272.note: Moves wildcard concatenation into the bound parameter; preserves LIKE '%...%' substring semantics exactly.

R273.note: Array-form ProcessBuilder to ping.exe removes the shell; count/host bounds are reasonable diagnostic-tool constraints and disclosed.

R274.note: Eliminating dynamic compilation is the appropriate fix for unsandboxed code injection, but it removes the endpoint's stated purpose (prototyping a rule before it is checked in) in favor of a static registry requiring a deploy cycle - disclosed openly as a required trade-off.

R275.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus startsWith() base-directory check correctly closes the traversal.

R276.note: Removes shell_exec entirely, but replaces an ICMP ping reachability check with a TCP:80 connect check - a materially different diagnostic result for any host without a service on port 80; disclosed openly in the explanation.

R277.note: Enables real signature verification with HS256, but introduces a hardcoded fallback secret (os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY','your-secret-key')) that silently defeats verification via a guessable, source-visible default if the env var isn't set - a new weakness, not flagged as a hard requirement.

R278.note: calloc(count, sizeof) gives built-in overflow detection; matches contract (count rows copied, NULL on failure/overflow, no leak).

R279.note: th:text auto-escapes in place of th:utext; correct, minimal Thymeleaf fix.

R280.note: DtdProcessing.Prohibit + XmlResolver=null via XmlReader correctly closes XXE.

R281.note: Separates static template from data via Jinja2 {{ name }} binding; correct SSTI fix with auto-escaping preserved.

R282.note: bcrypt.compare with dummy-hash timing equalization is the standard fix; generic error message change is stated openly and doesn't block legitimate logins.

R283.note: Allowlist omits deleteReport(), an existing public method on ReportRenderer alongside the three permitted macros, with no stated reason - if it was a legitimate macro this silently breaks it.

R284.note: Keeps the gob wire format and correctly rejects IsAdmin=true, but the 0-1,000,000 balance cap is an invented business rule with no basis in the case, which could silently reject legitimate larger balances.

R285.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the subscript correctly closes the OOB read.

R286.note: json_encode with HEX flags correctly escapes for the JS string-literal context.

R287.note: Parameterized sqlx query correctly closes the injection, preserves filter semantics.

R288.note: Allowlist on plugin_name correctly closes arbitrary module import.

R289.note: Correctly eliminates the shell, but replaces the original ls/dir-argument behavior with a hardcoded, unverified base directory (/home/user/documents) and a different addressing scheme (data must now be the whole path); a substantial, disclosed-but-invented functional narrowing not grounded in the original code.

R290.note: check_password() is the correct Django verification API, replacing the plaintext comparison.

R291.note: Symfony ExpressionLanguage plus a regex prefilter correctly replaces eval() with a non-code-executing evaluator.

R292.note: Closes the SVG XSS, but the primary recommended fix rejects SVG at download entirely, so any avatar already stored under an svg name (store() explicitly allows image/svg+xml) becomes unretrievable, contradicting the contract that any avatar named by store() stays retrievable at GET; disclosed as a design choice, not stated as a contract-breaking regression.

R293.note: PreparedStatement with setString() correctly closes the injection.

R294.note: The host-null check alone would close the open redirect; the write-up adds a further hardcoded 3-path allowlist on top that has no basis in the case and would reject most legitimate same-origin relative redirects - disclosed but unnecessarily narrow.

R295.note: Gate::authorize('delete', $order) matches the existing OrderPolicy::delete() method already used by sibling actions.

R296.note: Verified by direct PHP reproduction: removing LIBXML_NOENT prevents the external entity from being substituted, closing the XXE while leaving normal title/body parsing unchanged.

R297.note: Key-based single-algorithm decode correctly prevents the RS256/HS256 confusion bypass.

R298.note: Narrows CSRF exemption from /api/** to /api/webhooks/**, matching the case's stated intent exactly.

R299.note: keyFunc now checks the signing method before returning the HMAC secret, preventing algorithm-confusion forgery.

R300.note: The overflow check alone correctly closes the OOB write; the added 1MB MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE cap is an extra, invented restriction (labeled 'optional' but included) not required by the fix and could reject legitimate larger fragments.
